sections.h2: What are my choices for selling in Irving, TX?
sections.html:
An Irving owner has three main choices: a listing, a private sale, or an as-is cash offer. Condition, debt and timing usually decide.

Irving sits in western Dallas County on State Highways 183 and 114, about 12 miles west of downtown Dallas, between the Elm and West Forks of the Trinity River. The city's official site describes more than a quarter-million residents and a daytime population above 300,000, which gives sellers a large pool of employees looking for housing near work. Competing listings are plentiful, so price and condition decide how long a house sits.

  • A listing suits a house that is ready for the market.
  • A private sale avoids the listing fee and adds paperwork.
  • A cash sale skips repairs and showings.

Irving started as a rail town. Two surveyors for the Chicago, Rock Island and Gulf Railway bought 80 acres and held a lot auction on December 19, 1903, and voters incorporated the city in 1914, per the Handbook of Texas.

The population was 2,615 in 1950, 45,895 in 1960 and 100,996 by 1970, as farmland became subdivisions. Texas Stadium hosted the Dallas Cowboys from 1971 to 2008, Dallas-Fort Worth Airport grew along the western edge, and Las Colinas began on the north side. The same entry says Irving now has 8,500 businesses and ten Fortune 500 headquarters. The city says eight, so confirm current numbers on its site.

For a seller, the result is a mix of mid-century neighborhoods, newer Las Colinas areas and a lot of rental property, each with a different buyer pool.

sections.h2: What does Irving's economy mean for buyers of my house?
sections.html:
Irving's employment base is corporate. The city calls Las Colinas the Headquarters of Headquarters and reports eight Fortune 500 headquarters, while the Handbook of Texas says ten, and counts 8,500 businesses. The Handbook adds that Dallas-Fort Worth Airport runs along the city's western edge and that the University of Dallas, founded in 1956, and a Dallas College campus opened in 1977 are here.

That mix produces steady demand from relocating employees and renters, and it also means a lot of buyers work to a deadline. Sellers who can offer a firm closing date, clear title and move-in-ready condition tend to hold an advantage with that group.

The city's own site reports a population of 264,546, which differs from the Handbook's 2024 estimate of about 256,000, so quote the source you cite and check the date.

sections.h2: What city services and amenities help a seller in Irving?
sections.html:
Irving lists 92 parks, more than 33 miles of trails, three libraries and a municipal golf course, plus public transit options linking the city to the wider region. It also reports maintaining 1,440 lane miles of streets and an Aaa/AAA bond rating.

The city also reports that more than 60 percent of its general fund goes to public safety, and it lists four museums, three symphonies and the Irving Arts Center among its cultural draws. Those details help in listing copy, since buyers compare trail access, transit and park distance. The Handbook also notes that Irving has a council-manager form of government, so permit questions go to city staff. Check the city's pages for permits if you completed work such as a remodel or a deck, because an open permit can hold up a closing.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax on an Irving house?
sections.html:
Dallas County Tax Office handles collection for Irving. The downtown office is in the Records Building at 500 Elm Street, Suite 3300, the customer care line is 214-653-7811, and payments can be made online.

Its home page carries a notice that Dallas County adopted a rate that will raise more maintenance and operations taxes than last year, listed as an effective increase of 22.02 percent. The page also warns that payments not made by January 31, 2026 accrued an extra 7 percent in penalty and interest for the 2025 bills. Use the county site for current figures on your parcel.

sections.h2: What recording fees apply when an Irving deed is filed?
sections.html:
The Dallas County clerk records Irving deeds. This table reproduces the fee schedule in the Texas Courts manual.

First page$5.00

Ask the clerk for the total for your instrument, since fees can change.

sections.h2: What if tenants occupy my Irving house?
sections.html:
Irving has many more renters than owners, so sellers often deal with tenants. Texas calls for written notice to vacate, a short period of days unless the lease sets a different one, handed over in person, mailed, or e-mailed if the lease permits.

  • The landlord sues in justice court and the tenant is served before trial.
  • The hearing comes within a few weeks of filing.
  • An appeal to county court has a very short deadline after judgment.
  • A writ of possession follows a final judgment, with notice before removal.

Some covered properties fall under a longer federal notice. See counsel before you promise a buyer a vacant house.

sections.h2: Can a cash sale help with tax or lien problems in Irving?
sections.html:
It can, if the sale proceeds cover them at closing. A tax lien attaches in January and follows the house, so the closing agent will insist that unpaid taxes be resolved. The Comptroller adds that the January owner stays liable for that year's levy even after a sale.

Penalty and interest start on February 1 and a collection attorney's surcharge may follow, while some collectors offer installment plans on a homestead. Request a payoff figure from the Dallas County Tax Office, and have the closing agent confirm every lien before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What happens if an Irving owner dies without a will?
sections.html:
An heir who wants to sell must first show authority. A will is generally offered for probate within four years of death. With no will, a small estate affidavit can work for a modest estate when every heir agrees, and the court must approve it.

A transfer on death deed moves the house outside probate if it was recorded before the owner's death. An affidavit of heirship is another route, though buyers need not accept it. Heirs of an Irving house can ask a Dallas County probate lawyer which fits and then line up the paperwork before marketing.

sections.h2: Can adverse possession or squatters affect an Irving house?
sections.html:
In Texas, adverse possession means open and visible use of land under a claim hostile to the owner. A ten-year statute, section 16.026 of the Civil Practice and Remedies Code, applies, and a claim proceeds as a trespass to try title suit.

For an empty Irving house that has sat unattended, the practical risk is a squatter, not a title claim. Property Code chapter 24B offers an owner a removal request to the sheriff or constable, subject to conditions. Keeping vacant property secured, visited and insured is the better protection, and a quick sale can end the exposure.

faqs.a: Dallas County, in its western part, along State Highways 183 and 114.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Irving property taxes?
faqs.a: The Dallas County Tax Office, online or at its downtown Records Building at 500 Elm Street, Suite 3300.

faqs.q: What does the Dallas County clerk charge?
faqs.a: The manual prints a base charge per page and several smaller records fees. The clerk can give you an exact total.

faqs.q: How long is a Texas tenant's notice to vacate?
faqs.a: In writing, usually for a few days unless the lease says otherwise, and some covered properties fall under a longer federal notice.

faqs.q: Does unpaid tax follow the house to a buyer?
faqs.a: The lien stays with the property, so closing agents ask for payment at or before closing.
